entities.name: PMID:29032970
observations: Adult severe-burn cohort (n=145, TBSA>20%): day-3 platelet count combined with TBSA predicted sepsis with AUROC 0.779 (95% CI 0.697–0.862); reduced platelet peak predicted 50-day mortality, but persistence was not established as an independent sepsis predictor.

entities.name: PMID:41297233
observations: Retrospective cohort (n=55, TBSA>30%): day-3 platelet counts were 66 vs 120 ×10^9/L in septic versus nonseptic patients (p<0.001); a multivariable model achieved AUC 0.930, but platelet-specific adjusted effects were not reported.

entities.name: PMID:8418782
observations: Pediatric severe-burn case-control study: platelets <0.1 ×10^12/L for >4 days was associated with death; authors described platelet count as an independent predictor, but adjusted estimates and a clearly specified modern sepsis definition were unavailable.

entities.name: PMID:38535003
observations: Retrospective severe-burn study (n=90): thrombocytopenia persisted in septic nonsurvivors and tracked poor outcome; no validated sepsis-specific duration threshold or independent prediction estimate was reported.

entities.name: Persistent thrombocytopenia in burns
observations: In severe burns, low day-3 or nonrecovering platelet counts are clinically useful warning and severity/prognostic markers; current studies do not establish persistent thrombocytopenia as a validated independent predictor of incident sepsis.

Evidence is limited by retrospective small cohorts, confounding by burn severity/critical illness, inconsistent sepsis definitions, and absent platelet-specific adjusted estimates and external validation.

entities.name: MCL tear
observations: A blow to the lateral knee/leg can produce valgus stress and injure the medial collateral ligament; medial tenderness and valgus laxity at 30° support the diagnosis.
In the described sports injury, MCL sprain/partial tear is more likely than ACL rupture; catching can indicate concomitant meniscal injury.
